# A field guide to curiosity


Small experiments are a way of asking better questions. A useful tool begins with a real task, a clear constraint, and a willingness to try again.


## Start with something concrete


Choose one question. Make the smallest working version. Use it long enough to discover what the first sketch missed.


> The interesting part is what happens between the idea and the thing you can use.


## Three questions worth keeping


| Question | What it reveals |
| --- | --- |
| Who is this for? | The person, not the feature list |
| What can they do? | An outcome, not a promise |
| What can go wrong? | The boundary of the design |


## Keep the evidence


A short record of the choices, the compromises, and the result is often more useful than a long list of features.
